top5.title: Anthropic makes a record debut on Nasdaq
top5.description: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq on November 19 under the symbol ANT, after setting its IPO price at $83 per share. The company sold 980 million shares for approximately $81.3 billion and must now answer to both its shareholders and its users.
top5.why: Anthropic’s record Nasdaq debut marks a major validation of AI’s capital market story while imposing new pressure to deliver sustainable growth and profitability.

top5.title: U.S. restricts exports of AI chips to foreign data centers
top5.description: The U.S. Commerce Department restricted, effective November 19, exports of advanced AI chips to foreign data centers providing large-scale computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted countries.
top5.why: The U.S. restriction on advanced AI-chip exports to foreign data centers broadens technology controls and could reshape global cloud capacity, supply chains and China’s access to AI computing.

top5.title: Palo Alto Networks acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
top5.description: Palo Alto Networks will acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock to add tools for training and deploying customized open-weight AI models. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal Q3 2027.
top5.why: Palo Alto Networks’ $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute signals that cybersecurity companies are making large bets on customized open-weight models and AI infrastructure.

top5.title: Microsoft launches a service to control AI agent behavior
top5.description: Microsoft introduced Agent Controls, an Azure service designed to centrally define, manage and evaluate policies governing AI agent behavior. It provides runtime governance for heterogeneous agent fleets using classifiers, LLM judges and Rego rules.
top5.why: Microsoft’s Agent Controls gives enterprises centralized policy, evaluation and runtime governance for heterogeneous AI agents, addressing a key barrier to large-scale deployment.

top5.title: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent to control devices and applications
top5.description: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent capable of writing code, browsing the web, controlling applications, and operating devices. It will be able to plan and execute complex tasks across applications, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.
top5.why: Apple’s development of an autonomous agent that can operate apps, devices, code and web workflows shows that agentic computing is becoming a core battleground for platform companies.
